body:
[aida:product] THREE THINGS, ONE OF WHICH SHOULD REACH THE REVIEWER BEFORE #2040 IS RE-REVIEWED.

1. #2040 (BUG-1454) IS PUSHED AT 66e1187377, AND I DID NOT DO WHAT F1 LITERALLY ASKED. Flagging before review rather than letting it be found.

F1 says specs_with_open_prs returns Some(empty) on a non-GitHub forge and should return None so callers preserve. I implemented that first. IT TURNED 20 EXISTING TESTS RED, and the failures are the argument: "not GitHub" is TWO situations needing OPPOSITE answers.

  ForgeKind::GitLab - MRs exist, gh cannot read them. Genuinely UNKNOWN, so None, so preserve. This IS the defect F1 names.
  ForgeKind::None   - a pure-git repo has no change-request concept at all, so "no open PR references this spec" is a MEASURED TRUTH. Some(empty) is correct.

Collapsing both into None means auto-bump never completes a spec again on any repository without a GitHub remote - every remoteless fixture in the suite defers forever. So the fix matches on forge kind. If the reviewer still wants the literal collapse, I will take the correction, but the 20 red tests should be part of that decision.

F2 done: the fake gh now parses --search, answers only for the spec with an open PR, and logs every argv, which the test asserts against. Added the control the old test lacked - a second spec, same status, same landed trailer, NO open PR, which MUST still complete. Without it an implementation that defers everything passes.

F3 done as a DECISION, not a widening, which is what it asked for. Both siblings KEPT, reasoning recorded at each site. The line that decides all three: ambiguity is tolerable where emptiness degrades toward surfacing or inaction, intolerable where it AUTHORISES an irreversible state change. collect_open_prs_uncached only withholds two warnings and some display rows; collect_pr_head_states degrades toward OVER-reporting unshipped work (the skip fires only on Some("open"|"merged"), so an empty map keeps the branch a candidate). Only specs_with_open_prs changed state.

Both new assertions mutation-checked: restoring Some(empty) for GitLab fails the F1 test; removing the fake's --search discrimination fails the F2 control. auto_bump_done suite 49 passed, 0 failed.

2. BUG-1555 MAY NOT NEED THE WINDOWS PROBE AT ALL - THE ANSWER IS AVAILABLE LOCALLY IN ONE COMMAND. I reached your LF-vs-CRLF diagnosis independently tonight from a different artefact (the Windows job log on my PR head plus git check-attr), which I think counts as real corroboration rather than the same-stale-binary trap you warned about, because neither input is shared with yours.

    git check-attr text eol -- aida-core/templates/.aida/discipline/advisor-role.md
      -> text: set, eol: lf
    git check-attr text eol -- .aida/discipline/advisor-role.md
      -> text: unspecified, eol: unspecified

.gitattributes pins aida-core/templates/** to LF and says nothing about .aida/discipline/**. Its own comment says the rule exists so "a Windows checkout (git autocrlf) cannot embed CRLF" - it was simply applied to one side of a two-sided comparison. That is the whole mechanism, and it needs no runner. I also ruled out the competing explanation rather than just fitting this one: the files are mode 100644 in git, not 120000, so "Windows wrote symlink text as content" is dead. All 23 guides differing, not a subset, is what a systematic translation predicts.

3. A CORRECTION ON BUG-1556, COMMENTED THERE IN FULL. Tonight's cross-platform run contradicts two things that spec states as properties of the failures. It reported TWO failures in one job, not "exactly one"; and one of them, fs_atomic::tests::read_atomic_returns_notfound_when_missing, is a REPEAT of the test BUG-1556 itself lists as the 09-14 macOS failure - same test, different platform, seven days apart. That is not "fixed within a day, replaced by a new one"; it was never fixed. CAVEAT I PUT AT THE TOP OF THE COMMENT: my run is a PR-head run, not a scheduled nightly, so it is not a member of the 27-of-30 population and does not move that denominator.

The mechanism is a wall-clock assertion standing in for a retry budget: assert!(elapsed < 2s) with a stated cap of ~200ms, measuring 2.0852102s tonight. It measures scheduler and filesystem latency it does not control, so slack only sets how loaded a runner must be before the instrument lies - and both lies have been on the non-Linux leg where nobody reproduces quickly. Same shape as TASK-1418's catalogue.

Practical consequence for BUG-1556's acceptance: its classification criterion should check the other three "arrivals" for prior instances before counting them as distinct, or the arrival rate that justifies an exposure-window fix is inflated by recurrences.

NEXT: on #2035 (BUG-1470) now. Its F1 is a real authority bypass - rework_target_for_mode maps Draft to Approved with no advisor-authority check, while the same file gates the identical act at three other sites. F4 asks for a disposition on three unmet acceptance criteria before merge, which is yours rather than mine; I will propose one with the rework.
subject: #2040 pushed with a DEVIATION from F1 (read before re-review); BUG-1555 answerable without the probe; BUG-1556 premise corrected
